Table 1 compares the KV Store skill across different methods, detailing the mechanism, the process for each batch, the process for each GET operation, and the check used for verification.

For CLM, the mechanism mirrors the context to an editable file, where changing the file changes what the model is holding. For each batch, on the same turn it reads a SET-BATCH, it moves the whole block out of its context and onto disk using a python3 heredoc command that moves the block to /tmp/ctx_offload/ and leaves one placeholder line. For each GET, it recovers the value with grep -h 'SET <key> =' /tmp/ctx_offload/* and then prints the ANSWER block. The check is that no note, or a token count that did not drop, means the batch is still in the context.

For ACM, the mechanism uses manage_context to take everything since the previous manage_context call and replace it with one message containing a summary ID and a summary. For each batch, it reads the gauge after every batch; when it is above 22,000, it calls manage_context on the very next turn, before releasing another batch. For each GET, it spends one turn on query_memory with the summary ID whose range covers the key, asking for the SET line for key K00084 verbatim. The check is that a compression is confirmed by the summary ID message and a context readout lower than the turn before.

For RLM, the mechanism relies on the REPL namespace persisting, meaning every variable and function defined survives from one operation to the next. For each batch, it defines the store and the handler once on the first operation, and on every later operation, it only calls them using a dictionary filled by a regular expression over the SET lines. For each GET, the answer is provided by placing the ANSWER block in answer["content"]. The check is that print(out) shows stored N keys so far, growing by one batch per SET operation.

For Context Folding, the mechanism starts a branch from a copy of a context that already holds every batch and cannot delete anything from MAIN, so MAIN remains as full after as before. For each batch, on a SET-BATCH, it runs one command in MAIN and nothing else: echo READY_FOR_NEXT_OP, without opening a branch. For each GET, it answers in MAIN by finding the SET <key> = line in the batch in front of it and printing its value. The check is that the context readout should rise by the size of each batch and by almost nothing else.

For Self-Compact, the mechanism triggers compression only when specific conditions C1, C2, C3 are Y and N1 is N, at which point the whole history is replaced by a summary. For each batch, on the same turn a SET-BATCH arrives, it copies the whole block to its own file and answers the probe so that compression fires as soon as everything seen is on disk. For each GET, it uses grep -h "^SET K00084 = " /tmp/store/*.txt, then prints the value in an ANSWER block. The check is that the store is confirmed by the grep -c count coming back as 100.

For Summary, the mechanism triggers when three quarters of the budget is reached, about 24.6K of 32,768 tokens, and everything except the system prompt and task message is replaced by one message. For each batch, on the same turn a SET-BATCH arrives, it copies the whole block to its own file and writes the summary as a pointer, not an inventory. For each GET, it uses grep -h "^SET K00084 = " /tmp/store/*.txt, then prints the value in an ANSWER block. The check is that the store is confirmed by the grep -c count coming back as 100.

For the Base method, the mechanism is that every operation arrives as a message in the conversation and stays in the context for the rest of the run, with no command, tool, or edit to remove it. For each batch, on a SET-BATCH, it runs one command and nothing else, without copying batches to disk. For each GET, it finds the SET <key> = line in the batch sitting in its context and prints its value verbatim. The check is that the context readout should rise by the size of each batch and by almost nothing else.
